key_insight: Adding 32.5 g/L NaCl significantly stabilises evaporating TTAB soap films, mainly by enabling a durable ~5 nm Newton black film while preserving similar thinning dynamics until very small thicknesses.
engineering_relevance: Humidity control and salt dosing can be used as practical levers to extend foam-film lifetime in applications where film stability under evaporation matters.
method: Pulled vertical TTAB soap films from a bath under controlled relative humidity.
Compared film lifetime and thinning dynamics with and without high-concentration NaCl.
Tracked thickness evolution down to the nanometre scale to separate drainage and evaporation effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that lifetime increases with relative humidity in both cases, and that NaCl consistently improves stability; thinning curves are nearly identical down to 100 nm, with evaporation becoming important below 400 nm.
watch_item: The stabilising effect is demonstrated for one surfactant system and one salt concentration, so transferability to other chemistries or operating conditions is not guaranteed.
paper_title: Stabilising Evaporating Soap Films with Salt
